title: LDAEP and resting-state EEG in healthy women
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 69 healthy women (ages 19-40 years) acquired at the University of Oslo, featuring two complementary paradigms: loudness dependence of auditory evoked potentials (LDAEP) in 54 participants and resting-state recordings (eyes-open and eyes-closed) in all 69 participants. The study investigates the relationship between hormonal contraceptive use and central serotonergic activity, with concurrent collection of questionnaire data on contraceptive use, menstrual cycle phase, depressive symptoms, impulsivity, and lifestyle factors.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 Ag-AgCl electrodes positioned according to the extended 10-20 system (10-10) and 4 auxiliary oculogram channels, sampled at 2048 Hz. Resting-state recordings consisted of 4 minutes eyes-closed followed by 4 minutes eyes-open. LDAEP paradigm employed 1000 Hz tones at five intensity levels (55, 65, 75, 85, 95 dB SPL) with 80 trials per level. Raw data were stored in BrainVision format with standard software anti-aliasing filtering applied.
